links.comparator_used: Original PsyMetRiC model applied as-is (without recalibration or updating) to the Australian first-episode psychosis sample
links.outcome: Discrimination (C-statistic), calibration (observed vs predicted risk), and clinical usefulness (decision curve analysis) for predicting incident metabolic syndrome
links.effect: Original partial model C = 0.71 (95% CI 0.64-0.75) and full model C = 0.72 (95% CI 0.65-0.77) with consistent under-prediction of risk; after recalibration and updating, C-statistics slightly improved, agreement between observed and predicted risk greatly improved, and the window of likely clinical usefulness improved significantly (specific post-update values not given in the abstract)
links.quote: Recalibration and updating led to slightly improved C-statistics, greatly improved agreement between observed and predicted risk, and a narrow window of likely clinical usefulness improved significantly.

design_hint: local validation and recalibration before deployment
